scenario.title: 跟朋友討論換工作
scenario.context: 考慮離職時，常會比較過去和現在：「我以前很喜歡這份工作」「我還是不習慣加班」「我慢慢習慣了」。used to、be used to、get used to 看起來很像，意思卻完全不同，是台灣人最常搞混的一組。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: I think I'm done with my job.
lines.zh: 我覺得我受夠我的工作了。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: What? You used to love it!

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: I did. I used to look forward to Mondays. Now I dread them.
lines.zh: 是啊。我以前很期待星期一，現在超怕。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: New management. I'm working until ten every night, and I'm just not used to it.
lines.zh: 新管理層。我每天都工作到十點，實在不習慣。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: That sounds exhausting. You sound completely burnt out.
lines.zh: 聽起來好累，你聽起來完全燃燒殆盡了。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: I am. And there's no promotion in sight. It feels like a dead-end job.
lines.zh: 是啊，而且完全看不到升遷，感覺是份沒前途的工作。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: A little. A startup offered me a job, but I'm scared to jump ship.
lines.zh: 有一點。一家新創給我 offer，但我不敢跳槽。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: I'm used to having a stable paycheck. I'm not sure I could get used to all that uncertainty.
lines.zh: 我習慣有穩定的薪水了，我不確定能不能適應那麼多不確定性。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: You'd get used to it. I did when I started freelancing.
lines.zh: 你會習慣的，我剛開始接案時也是。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: True. But what if the grass isn't actually greener?
lines.zh: 也對。但如果那邊其實也沒比較好呢？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Then at least you'll know. Staying somewhere that makes you miserable isn't safe either.
lines.zh: 那至少你會知道。待在讓你痛苦的地方也不叫安全。

patterns.en: I used to love this job.
I'm ready for a new challenge.
patterns.zh: 我準備好迎接新挑戰了。

chinglish.wrong: I used to work overtime now.
chinglish.right: I'm used to working overtime now.
chinglish.why: used to + V 是「以前常…（現在不了）」。「習慣」要用 be used to + V-ing。

chinglish.wrong: I am used to work overtime.
chinglish.why: be used to 的 to 是介系詞，後面接 V-ing（複習第 14 單元：介系詞後接 V-ing）。

chinglish.wrong: I want to resign my job.
chinglish.right: I want to quit my job. / I'm going to resign.
chinglish.why: resign 通常不直接接 my job，說 resign from 或 quit。口語最常說 quit。

chinglish.wrong: I use to live in Tainan.
chinglish.right: I used to live in Tainan.
chinglish.why: 肯定句一定是 used to。只有在 did 後面才用 use to：Did you use to…?

grammar.title: used to / be used to / get used to
grammar.oneLiner: used to + V = 以前常（現在不了）；be used to + V-ing = 習慣；get used to + V-ing = 逐漸習慣。
whenToUse: used to + 原形：過去的習慣或狀態，現在已經不是了。I used to love Mondays.
否定和問句：didn't use to / Did you use to…?（沒有 d）
be used to + 名詞 / V-ing：已經習慣。I'm used to working late.
get used to + 名詞 / V-ing：逐漸習慣的過程。You'll get used to it.
be / get used to 可以用各種時態：I'm getting used to it. / I've gotten used to it.
判斷訣竅：後面是原形就是「以前」；後面是 V-ing 或名詞就是「習慣」。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 三個結構都有 used to，但意思和後面接的東西都不一樣。中文的「以前」和「習慣」是完全不同的詞，所以台灣人很難從字面分辨。另外 be used to 的 to 是介系詞，後面要接 V-ing，這一點特別反直覺，因為我們習慣 to 後面接原形。

examples.correct: I used to work at a bank.
examples.note: 以前在銀行工作，現在沒有。

examples.correct: I'm used to waking up early.
examples.incorrect: I'm used to wake up early.

examples.correct: It took me a year to get used to the new system.
Did you use to live in Kaohsiung?
examples.incorrect: Did you used to live in Kaohsiung?

examples.correct: I didn't use to like coffee, but now I love it.

quiz.question: I ___ play basketball every day, but now I don't have time.
quiz.explanation: 以前常做、現在不了：used to + 原形。

quiz.question: I've lived in Taipei for years, so I'm used to ___ the MRT.
Don't worry. You'll get used to ___ (work) from home.
"I'm used to spicy food" means:
options: I ate spicy food in the past.
Spicy food is normal for me.
I'm starting to like spicy food.

slang.usage: 長期壓力導致身心疲憊。名詞 burnout。美式也拼 burned out。

risk.note: 現在是很正式被承認的概念，跟主管或 HR 講也可以。

examples.en: After three years of overtime, I was completely burnt out.
examples.zh: 加班三年後，我完全燃燒殆盡了。

examples.en: Take a break before you burn out.

slang.usage: 突然離開公司或團隊，常帶「在困難時離開」的意味。

risk.note: 說別人 jump ship 可能暗示不忠誠。

examples.en: Half the team jumped ship after the merger.
examples.zh: 合併後團隊一半的人跳槽了。

examples.en: I'm not ready to jump ship yet.

slang.meaning: 更好的機會、更好的地方
slang.usage: leave for greener pastures = 離開去找更好的機會。相關俗語：The grass is always greener on the other side.（外國的月亮比較圓）

examples.en: She left for greener pastures in Singapore.
examples.zh: 她去新加坡找更好的發展了。

examples.en: Remember, the grass isn't always greener on the other side.
examples.zh: 記住，別人家的草不一定比較綠。

slang.usage: 沒有升遷、沒有成長空間的工作。

risk.note: 說別人的工作是 dead-end 很失禮。

examples.en: I spent five years in a dead-end job before I went back to school.
examples.zh: 我在一份沒前途的工作待了五年才回去念書。

examples.en: No job is a dead-end if you're learning something.
examples.zh: 只要還在學習，沒有工作是沒前途的。

review.question: My old boss, ___ I really respected, retired last year.
review.explanation: 複習第 57 單元：非限定子句不用 that（whom / who 當受詞）。

review.question: By next March, I ___ have worked here for five years.
review.explanation: 複習第 56 單元：未來完成式。

review.question: Which is the softest?
options: You might want to think about other options.
review.explanation: 複習第 54 單元：軟化語氣。

review.question: By the time I quit, I ___ there for six years.
review.explanation: 複習第 50 單元：過去完成式。

review.question: I ___ about quitting for months.
review.explanation: 複習第 26 單元：完成進行式。
